necessary_context.content: The standing manifold is complete and d-dimensional. A g-convex set contains the unique minimizing geodesic between every pair of its points. A function is g-convex along those geodesics and M-Lipschitz in distance. A subgradient g at x satisfies f(y) >= f(x)+<g,log_x(y)> for every y in the domain. Each first-order query returns f(x) and a subgradient. A Riemannian halfspace is {y:<g,log_x(y)> <= 0}.
necessary_context.locator: PDF p.2, §1 definitions and black-box model
necessary_context.name: Definitions and Oracle

necessary_context.content: For sectional curvatures in [-K,K], a g-convex closed ball D=Bbar(x_ref,r), and a g-convex M-Lipschitz f on D, the question asks for a deterministic first-order method that, for every epsilon in (0,1), finds x with f(x)-min_D f <= epsilon M r using O(poly(zeta,d) log(1/epsilon)) Oracle queries and poly(zeta,d) arithmetic per iteration, where zeta=(r sqrt(K))/tanh(r sqrt(K)). This is an open question, not an established general-manifold result.
necessary_context.name: Open Question 1 scope

necessary_context.content: Section 2 sketches a local-to-global reduction and explains the local geodesic-map procedure for hyperbolic space, normalizing curvature to -1. The sphere analysis is explicitly omitted. Section 3 describes obstacles for tangent-space ellipsoid transfer and halfspace-/volume-preserving maps.
necessary_context.name: Constant-curvature specialization

observed_source_issues.description: The printed local tolerance is epsilon M R/4 and T=ceil((2r/R) log(2/epsilon)); the resulting global gap is printed as <= epsilon, whereas Open Question 1 uses epsilon M r. No silent normalization repair is made.

The map is defined as phi_k:H^d -> B(0,1), but transformed domains repeatedly use phi_k^{-1}(D). These expressions are not type-consistent with that definition. The text also calls a displayed objective sublevel set a Riemannian halfspace. No corrected formula is asserted as a verified result.
